title: V-I Characteristics of PN Junction Diode
aim: To plot forward and reverse bias characteristics of a PN junction diode and determine cut-in voltage and dynamic resistance.
theory: A PN junction diode conducts easily in forward bias once the barrier potential (approx 0.7V for Silicon) is exceeded. In reverse bias, only a tiny reverse saturation current flows until breakdown occurs.
observationFormat: Forward Bias: Voltage Vf (V) vs Current If (mA); Reverse Bias: Voltage Vr (V) vs Current Ir (uA)
conclusionNote: The forward cut-in voltage for Silicon diode was observed to be approximately 0.65V.
safetyNotes: Do not exceed diode rated current (1A for 1N4007). Ensure correct polarity before powering RPS.

title: Half Wave and Full Wave Rectifiers
aim: To construct half-wave and center-tapped full-wave rectifiers and calculate ripple factor and efficiency.
theory: Rectification is the conversion of alternating current to direct current. A half-wave rectifier uses one diode while a center-tapped full-wave rectifier uses two diodes conducting alternately on opposite half cycles.
observationFormat: Table of Input Vac, Output Vdc, Vrms, Ripple Factor (gamma) with and without filter capacitor.
conclusionNote: Center-tapped full-wave rectifier exhibits higher efficiency and lower ripple factor compared to half wave rectifier.
safetyNotes: Discharge filter capacitors before handling circuit connections.

title: Linear and Circular Convolution of Sequences
aim: To compute linear and circular convolution of two discrete time sequences using MATLAB / Code Composer Studio.
theory: Convolution is a mathematical operation that expresses the output of a Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) system given its impulse response and input signal. Linear convolution of lengths N1 and N2 yields length N1+N2-1.
observationFormat: Input sequences x[n] and h[n], analytical linear convolution y[n], circular convolution result.
conclusionNote: Verified that linear convolution matches circular convolution when sequences are zero-padded to length N1+N2-1.
safetyNotes: Ensure DSP workstation audio outputs are properly terminated.

title: 8086 Arithmetic Operations and Block Transfer
aim: To write and execute an 8086 assembly language program for 16-bit addition, subtraction, multiplication, and block memory transfer.
theory: The 8086 microprocessor is a 16-bit CPU with a 20-bit address bus. Memory segmentation divides memory into code, data, stack, and extra segments.
observationFormat: Registers AX, BX, CX, DX, SI, DI states before and after instruction execution; Memory dump of target block.
conclusionNote: Successfully verified arithmetic operations and block memory movement on 8086 trainer kit.
safetyNotes: Avoid static discharge when handling trainer kit bus expansion pins.

title: CMOS Inverter DC Characteristics
aim: To design, simulate, and observe the voltage transfer characteristics (VTC) of a static CMOS inverter and compute noise margins.
theory: A CMOS inverter consists of an nMOS pull-down and a pMOS pull-up network. In steady-state, one transistor is off, yielding near-zero static power dissipation. Noise margins NMH and NML quantify immunity against noise.
observationFormat: Input Vin (V) vs Output Vout (V); Noise margins NMH and NML; Switching threshold Vm.
conclusionNote: Verified switching threshold Vm approximately Vdd/2 and calculated noise margins.
safetyNotes: Ensure ESD precautions when touching FPGA or CMOS boards.

title: 4-Bit Ripple Carry Adder on FPGA
aim: To implement a 4-bit ripple carry adder using Verilog HDL, simulate testbench, synthesize, and verify on FPGA development board.
theory: A 4-bit ripple carry adder cascades 4 full adders where the carry output of each stage feeds the carry input of the next stage. It calculates Sum[3:0] and CarryOut.
observationFormat: Inputs A[3:0], B[3:0], Cin; Outputs Sum[3:0], Cout displayed on board LEDs.
conclusionNote: Verified all 16 test vectors on Spartan-6 FPGA board with switch inputs and LED outputs.
safetyNotes: Power down the FPGA board before altering jumper connections.
